title: Set a dtype
summary: A dtype specifies how numbers are represented. Floating-point tensors are commonly used for model calculations and gradients.
introduction: A dtype specifies how numbers are represented. Floating-point tensors are commonly used for model calculations and gradients. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A dtype specifies how numbers are represented. Floating-point tensors are commonly used for model calculations and gradients.

blocks.code:
import torch

x = torch.tensor([1, 2], dtype=torch.float32)
print(x.dtype)
blocks.title: Set a dtype

blocks.text: The output is torch.float32. Both values use that type.

blocks.text: Integer tensors cannot be used for every gradient calculation.
